summary: Ran the molecular tests for M1-S03 (run 3, the S2-F-04/S2-F-05 rebuild) in build tier2-webhook: both always-on structural checks and all three declared checker acceptance tests pass, check-outputs confirms all 20 declared outputs present, and the two run-3 source fixes (URL.getOrgDomainUrl replacing the removed getSalesforceBaseUrl; the LongTextArea WHERE-filter replaced by select-then-pick helpers) are mechanically confirmed present in the artefacts under test. The step's manual acceptance test is deferred to the M1 gate; its clause (b) still names templates/apex/HttpClient.cls, a template dropped under remedy B and never shipped by this step, though the security property it is testing for is independently verified true by inspection. Status set to tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual (Step 7 HIGH row): both always-on checks (xml, manifest) completed, all three declared checkers exited 0 from an exit code this agent observed directly, check-outputs reported ok:true with no missing/empty/malformed paths, and the manual test was classified against the Given/When/Then testability bar rather than skipped. No command test was refused, no manifest exclusion was needed, and check-outputs reported nothing missing -- none of the MEDIUM or LOW triggers in Step 7 fired.

process_observations.observation: All three declared checkers exit 0 with zero findings at any severity, not merely zero blocking findings, on the run-3 artefacts.

check-outputs confirms all 20 declared outputs for M1-S03 exist, are non-empty, and (for the 12 XML files among them) parse, and all 12 files are brace/paren/bracket/string balanced under a mechanical scan.

Both run-3 fixes are verifiably present in the source text under test rather than only asserted in deploy-order.md's narrative: getOrgDomainUrl replaces getSalesforceBaseUrl at both call sites, and IntegrationFailureResendTest.cls no longer filters SOQL on the LongTextArea field Request_Payload__c.

No checker in this loop compiles Apex, and this step has still never been compiled: run 2 passed every declared checker plus the xml parse and brace-balance scan and then failed the org on two faults (a removed-after-58.0 method name, a filter on an unfilterable LongTextArea field) invisible to all of them, and run 3 has not yet been through mock_deploy.py.

The manual acceptance test's clause (b) names templates/apex/HttpClient.cls as the endpoint-composition mechanism, but that template was dropped under remedy B before run 2 and is not shipped by run 2 or run 3, so a reviewer ticking the clause literally would find the named file absent even though the security property it tests is independently true.

M1-S03 ships no templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls / TriggerControl kill switch, so a bulk data load reassigning Case ownership into the Tier_2_Engineering queue would escalate every affected Case with no bypass; this is a build-level decision recorded in deploy-order.md section 4, not a defect in this run's tests.
Whether the org already has an after-update trigger on Case is not settled by any of the build's 45 clarifications, and CaseTrigger.trigger assumes none exists.

Now that M1-S03 is tested, build-doc-keeper should record the manual test's stale HttpClient clause, the missing trigger kill switch, and the manifest Apex-exception note into decisions.md and traceability.md.
